summary: The note describes how Maplewood Heights overhauled its waste management and recycling from September 2023 to March 2024. A citizen-led coalition used data, education, a color-coded bin system, smart bins and facility investment to raise recycling rates from 15% to 65% and cut landfill waste. The changes also saved the city money, and the community is now presented as a model for others.
one_line: Maplewood Heights raised recycling from 15% to 65% in under a year through a coalition, education, color-coded bins, smart bins and infrastructure investment.
key_facts: Before September 2023, Maplewood Heights had a recycling rate of just 15% and landfills were nearing capacity.
The Maplewood Sustainability Coalition was formed on September 15, 2023, led by Dr. Henry Clarkson, an environmental studies professor.
The coalition's research found that 40% of waste sent to landfills was recyclable.
An education campaign began in October 2023 with workshops, school programs, and guides distributed to every household.
On December 1, 2023, Maplewood Heights introduced color-coded bins: blue for recyclables (paper, plastic, glass) and green for organic waste.
Audits by the recycling committee, including Maria Gonzalez, reported a 50% reduction in recycling contamination after the bin system launched.
By February 2024, smart recycling bins with sensors that reject improperly sorted materials were introduced; Alex Duran helped with the software setup.

A $1.5 million investment in the local recycling facility in early 2023 let it handle increased volume; manager Laura Chen reports a 25% increase in recyclable input and a 30% cut in processing costs.
As of March 2024, overall waste production fell 10% year over year and waste sent to landfills dropped 20%.
Recycling rates reached 65%, described as a 50% increase in just under a year.
The city saved approximately $200,000 in landfill fees and earned an extra $150,000 selling higher-quality recyclables.
City Treasurer Ellen Suarez plans to put the savings back into community sustainability projects.
Ongoing projects include expanding the fleet of smart bins and introducing incentives for household composting.
